transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I keep hearing the bank and bill collectors talking about me, like they’re sending me messages that I’ve ruined everything, even when no one else hears anything. It's just... it's terrifying because my wife swears there's no one there, but I hear them so clearly.
Have you been experiencing any unusual beliefs or thoughts that you think might not be true, such as thinking you're in danger or that someone is out to get you, in addition to hearing these voices?

I'm convinced the bank and the power company are keeping a file on me and working together to secretly shame me through every bill they send, even though my wife says they're normal. I also feel like our neighbors are in on a plan to expose me as a failure, which makes me terrified to leave the house. It's deeply embarrassing, but I can't stop believing it's true.
Can you tell me more about how these voices and beliefs started, and if they seem to be related to each other in a way that makes sense to you, or if they feel more disjointed and unrelated?

They started about seven months ago, but only after I had already been feeling deeply depressed, worthless, and completely overwhelmed by our money problems. To me, they feel totally connected because the voices and the bills are both about the bank and collectors targeting me, calling me a fraud for ruining my family's finances.

Do you ever hear these voices or have these thoughts when you're not thinking about your financial situation or feeling depressed, or are they always triggered by something related to your money problems or low mood?

No, I never experienced anything like this back when I was working and feeling like myself. They only started after I fell into this deep depression and the money problems piled up. They are always tied to how low I'm feeling and my worries about our finances.

Can you describe a typical day and how these voices and beliefs affect your daily functioning and interactions with others, and do you feel like you're able to distinguish what's real and what might be part of your depression or these delusional thoughts?

A typical day for me is just sitting alone in the garage for hours doing nothing, terrified to answer the phone and leaving my wife to handle all the bills and chores because I'm too ashamed to face anyone. Even though my wife tells me she doesn't hear anything and shows me the bills are normal, these voices and messages feel one hundred percent real to me. I just can't shake the belief that they are targeting me and that I've completely failed.

Do you think these voices and beliefs would go away if your financial situation improved and you were no longer feeling depressed, or do you believe they would persist regardless of changes in your mood or circumstances?

I really hope they would go away, because I never experienced anything like this back when I was working and feeling like myself. Since they only started after I fell into this deep depression and the bills piled up, I believe they would finally stop if my mood lifted and our money problems were resolved. It's just exhausting living with this every day.

You mentioned that these voices and beliefs started after you became depressed and had financial problems. Do you think the voices and beliefs are a direct result of your depression, or do you feel they are separate issues that just happen to coincide with your low mood?

I feel like they are directly connected to my depression, because I never had these voices or beliefs back when I was working and feeling like myself. They only started after months of feeling deeply down, worthless, and overwhelmed by our financial stress. Since the voices are always talking about the bills and me being a failure, they feel completely tied to my low mood.

You've mentioned that the voices and beliefs seem to be connected to your feelings of depression and financial stress, but can you tell me if there are any times when the content of the voices or the nature of these beliefs seems to shift or change, perhaps becoming more or less intense in relation to your mood or specific events?

No, the content doesn't really change; it's always the same voices accusing me of being a fraud and a failure who ruined our lives. Because I feel so deeply down and stuck every single day, the intensity just stays constantly heavy and never really lets up.

Do you think the voices and beliefs about being a failure and the bank and collectors targeting you would still be present if your depression were treated and you were no longer feeling down, or are they so closely tied to your mood that they would likely disappear with improvement in your depression?

I believe they would disappear because they are completely tied to how down I feel. I never experienced anything like these terrifying voices or thoughts back when I was working and feeling like myself; they only started after months of feeling deeply depressed and worthless over our finances. I really hope that if the depression is treated and this heavy cloud lifts, those voices will finally go away too.

If your depression were successfully treated and you no longer felt down, do you think the voices and beliefs about the bank and collectors targeting you would still make sense to you, or would they seem irrational and unrelated to your reality?

I think they probably wouldn't make sense anymore, because I never experienced anything like this before my injury when I was feeling like my normal self. These voices and beliefs only started after I fell into this deep depression and felt like a complete failure. If the depression finally went away, I don't think these terrifying thoughts and voices would happen either.

If you were to have a day where your mood significantly improved, perhaps due to a positive event or a good response to treatment, do you think the voices and delusional beliefs about the bank and collectors would also improve or lessen in intensity, or would they remain unaffected by your mood change?

Yes, I think they would definitely lessen or even stop completely if my mood improved, because they seem to feed off how down and hopeless I feel. I never had any of these terrifying voices or ideas when I was feeling like my normal self before the depression hit. If my mood were to get better, I believe those messages would finally fade away.

If your mood were to significantly improve and you no longer felt depressed, do you think the voices and beliefs about the bank and collectors targeting you would still be present and make sense to you, or would they seem irrational and disappear?

I never experienced anything like these voices or beliefs before I fell into this dark place and became deeply depressed. If I could somehow get back to feeling like my old self and lift this heavy mood, I believe those terrifying messages would probably go away too. They just wouldn't make sense to me anymore if I felt normal again.
